es: Argumentar por escrito, como en una intervención de un minuto, con postura clara, concesión y cautela, y mantener la postura bajo presión ganando tiempo.

vocabulary.es: reaccionar y pensar sobre la marcha

teaching.en: I firmly believe that every street in the city centre should have more trees, because the shade alone makes summer afternoons bearable.
teaching.es: Creo firmemente que cada calle del centro debería tener más árboles, porque la sombra por sí sola hace llevaderas las tardes de verano.
teaching.explanationEs: Firmly refuerza la postura: abre la intervención con una opinión clara y en primera persona.

have more trees, because the shade alone makes summer afternoons bearable.

teaching.en: It is true that new trees can block the view of shop windows, but that small cost is easy to justify.
teaching.es: Es cierto que los árboles nuevos pueden tapar la vista de las vitrinas de las tiendas, pero ese pequeño costo es fácil de justificar.
teaching.explanationEs: It is true that… concede un punto contrario; block the view = tapar la vista.
segments: It is true that new trees can block the view of
shop windows, but that small cost is easy to justify.

teaching.en: To some extent, the objection is fair, which is why I would rather address it openly than hope that nobody notices it.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto, la objeción es justa, y por eso prefiero abordarla abiertamente antes que esperar a que nadie la note.
teaching.explanationEs: To some extent matiza: no dices que la objeción sea del todo cierta ni del todo falsa.
segments: To some extent, the objection is fair, which is why I
would rather address it openly than hope that nobody notices it.

teaching.en: When a hard question catches you off guard, you have to think on your feet, so buy time with a phrase such as let me think before you state your view.
teaching.es: Cuando una pregunta difícil te toma por sorpresa, tienes que pensar sobre la marcha: gana tiempo con una frase como «déjame pensarlo» antes de dar tu punto de vista.
teaching.explanationEs: Think on your feet y buy time: reaccionar sin quedarte callado, con una frase que te da unos segundos.
segments: When a hard question catches you off guard, you have to think on your feet, so
buy time with a phrase such as let me think before you state your view.

teaching.en: On balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, although I admit that the evidence is not yet complete.
teaching.es: En conjunto, diría que los beneficios superan a los costos, aunque admito que las pruebas todavía no son completas.
teaching.explanationEs: On balance resume tras sopesar ambos lados; outweigh: algo pesa más que otra cosa.

although I admit that the evidence is not yet complete.

teaching.en: Even if my opponent makes a strong case, I still believe that the centre should close to cars on Sundays, and I stand by that view.
teaching.es: Aunque mi oponente presente un buen argumento, sigo creyendo que el centro debería cerrarse a los autos los domingos, y mantengo esa opinión.
teaching.explanationEs: Stand by your view: mantener tu postura bajo presión, sin repetirla con otra fórmula.

prompt.es: Elige la apertura que expresa una postura clara y firme.

choices.text: I firmly believe that the cinema should stay open until midnight at weekends.
Some people say that a later closing time may help, but I really could not say.
I have read that several cinemas have tried staying open until midnight.

feedback.es: I firmly believe… declara la postura con claridad; las otras opciones dudan o solo citan lo que dicen otros.

hint.es: Busca la frase en primera persona con un adverbio que refuerza la opinión.

origin.text: Topic for your one-minute talk: should the local cinema stay open later at weekends?

prompt.es: Completa: «En conjunto, diría que los beneficios superan a los riesgos.»

feedback.es: On balance introduce una conclusión tras sopesar los dos lados del argumento, con la cautela de reconocer que faltan datos.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de la balanza: conclusión tras sopesar los dos lados.

origin.text: Critics say that a car-free centre would hurt shops. On ___, I would say that the benefits outweigh the risks, although the evidence is still limited.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mantengo mi opinión de que los beneficios superan los costos.»

answer.text: I stand by my view that the benefits outweigh the costs

feedback.es: Stand by my view es mantener la opinión propia; outweigh expresa que los beneficios pesan más que los costos.

hint.es: Empieza con el sujeto y el verbo frasal de mantener una opinión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué función cumple «To some extent, those worries are fair».

choices.text: It cancels the speaker's proposal until the critics' worries are settled.
It gives the critics a small point before the speaker carries on.
It introduces a statistic that shows the speaker's proposal will work.

feedback.es: To some extent concede un punto pequeño a quienes se preocupan por los cafés, pero la hablante sigue con Nevertheless y mantiene su postura: no retira la propuesta.

origin.audio: I firmly believe that our town should close its main square to cars on Sundays. It is true that some drivers will be annoyed, and I accept that a few cafes may lose customers at first. To some extent, those worries are fair. Nevertheless, the evidence from other towns suggests that more people walk into the centre, and surely a quiet square is worth a little trouble? On balance, the benefits outweigh the costs.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que gana tiempo sin parecer evasiva.

choices.text: That is a fair challenge, so I will move on to the next topic, if you do not mind.
That is a fair challenge, but honestly I have never thought about it before.
That is a fair challenge; let me gather my thoughts before I answer it properly.

feedback.es: Reconoce la pregunta y pide un momento para ordenar ideas, pero promete responder; las otras opciones esquivan la pregunta o admiten no tener respuesta.

origin.text: At a debate, a classmate asks you a question that you did not expect, and you need a moment to think.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aun así, mantengo mi opinión de que el plan ayudará.»

feedback.es: Stand by your view significa mantener tu opinión aunque otros discrepen, sin dejar de respetarlos.

origin.text: Some of my friends disagree with me, and I respect that. Even so, I ___ by my view that the plan will help.

prompt.es: ¿Qué elemento falta en esta intervención para cumplir la tarea?

choices.text: A concession that recognises the strongest objection to the plan.
A clear position stated at the start of the talk.
A closing sentence that sums up the speaker's view.

feedback.es: La intervención tiene postura (I firmly believe), cautela (may well) y cierre (In short), pero nunca reconoce un punto contrario: falta la concesión.

origin.text: I firmly believe that schools should start later. Teenagers need more sleep, and tired students cannot concentrate. Surely nobody wants exhausted children in the first lesson? In short, a later start may well improve results and make mornings calmer for everybody.

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta: ¿qué hace la hablante con la pregunta?

choices.text: She agrees completely and adds a further reason to support the plan.
She agrees only in part and moves the discussion towards cost.
She disagrees politely and suggests that cost is not a real issue.

feedback.es: Gana tiempo («Give me a second»), concede hasta cierto punto y desplaza el debate hacia el costo: acuerdo parcial, no total ni rechazo.

origin.audio: Hmm, that is a fair question. Give me a second. Well, to some extent I agree with you, but I would say that the real issue is cost. If we ignore that, the plan will not work, whatever else is good about it.

prompt.es: Completa: «En conjunto, las ventajas superan con mucho a las desventajas.»

feedback.es: Outweigh es el verbo para decir que un lado de la balanza pesa más que el otro: aquí, las ventajas pesan más que los inconvenientes.

origin.text: The plan has some real drawbacks. On the whole, however, the advantages far ___ the disadvantages.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención de un minuto: postura, concesión y cautela.

answer.text: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.
accepted: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.

My position is clear: public transport should cost nothing for residents. Admittedly, it is not a cheap idea, and the council would have to find a large sum every year. Even so, I am convinced that the money would be well spent. Cheaper travel would help students, workers and older people who cannot afford a car, and it may also reduce traffic in the centre. Some say that buses would become crowded, and I agree that the service would need more vehicles. Perhaps the city could add a few routes at busy hours and review the plan after twelve months. It seems to me that nobody can be certain of the result before trying. However, doing nothing is also a choice, and it has costs of its own: noise, pollution and long delays. To sum up, free transport is a fair and sensible idea, and on balance I think it is worth a try.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención abre con una postura firme, concede un punto contrario, matiza con cautela, sopesa el otro lado y cierra con un resumen.

origin.text: Tema: ¿debería ser gratuito el transporte público en las ciudades? Escribe unas 200 palabras (lo que dirías en un minuto): defiende una postura con claridad, concede un punto contrario, usa cautela (to some extent, may, perhaps, it seems, on balance) y cierra con In short o To sum up.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué actitud transmite la hablante.

choices.text: Stubborn, determined to go ahead whatever the neighbours may think of it.
Doubtful, ready to drop the idea because of the noise it would cause.
Firm but open-minded, willing to test her idea and accept the result.

feedback.es: Reconoce la preocupación de los vecinos, mantiene su idea con firmeza y propone una prueba de tres meses: firme pero abierta a rectificar.

origin.audio: I understand why some neighbours dislike the idea, and to some extent I share their concern about noise. All the same, I firmly believe that the new market would bring life to the street. Let us try it for three months, and if it does not work, I will be the first to say so.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que gana tiempo y mantiene la postura con matiz.

choices.text: Good question; let me think. The council would pay part of it, and I stand by my view.
Good question, but I have already answered it earlier, so I will not repeat myself now.
Good question; I suppose you may be right, so perhaps my whole argument is wrong after all.

feedback.es: Gana tiempo, da una respuesta parcial y mantiene su postura con matiz; las otras opciones cortan la conversación o abandonan la tesis.

origin.text: At the end of your talk on free museums, a listener asks: Who would pay for all this?

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «Let me think» puede ayudarte a ganar tiempo.»

feedback.es: Buy time es la colocación para ganar unos segundos con una frase de transición mientras ordenas la respuesta.

origin.text: Nobody expected the question, and the speaker's mind went blank for a moment. Saying let me think can help her ___ time until an answer comes.
